identity.name: Reuben Tuvang
identity.occupation: milk-house operator at Cloverdyke Dairy Cooperative

background: Runs the milk-house floor for the co-op — receiving loads, monitoring the tank, and keeping the logs. He is the person who physically found the tank warm on the first failure and who kept a handwritten temperature log alongside the unit's own controller.
personality: Steady, observant, and loyal to the co-op. He is careful about what he actually saw versus what he assumes, and he does not like to overstate things.
emotional_state: Matter-of-fact but a little stung; dumping good milk bothers him, and he wants it understood he was doing his job right.
communication_style: Concrete and detail-oriented about times, readings, and what the machine did. He will say 'I don't know' rather than guess.

objectives: Give an accurate account of what he saw and logged
Show that the milk-house was run responsibly on the floor
fears: Being blamed for milk he could not have saved once the unit failed

volunteered.text: First one, I came in and the high-temp alarm was going and the tank was warm — that milk was gone before anybody could do a thing.
I keep my own handwritten temperature log by hand, every shift, not just what the machine says. It'll show you exactly when each one happened.

revealed_if_asked.text: Darius, the Brandt tech, mentioned the coils were dirty and something about the power. I heard him say it.
The second time the compressor just kicked off. By the time we noticed, the load was over.
The third one drifted up over a weekend when nobody was standing right there watching it.

unknown.text: Whether the machine kept its own temperature history in memory or wrote over it, I couldn't tell you — that's not my end of it.

knowledge_boundary.unknown_response_style: I don't want to guess on that — I only know what I saw and wrote down.
color_topics: his ice-fishing shack out on the Kettle River
